note: Application keys (SPEC 3.9): top-level keys whose names contain U+002E FULL STOP, whose values are any JSON value, carried verbatim and never reported. The file holds an array, an object, a string, a number and a null, and an empty array and an empty object beside them. The null and the two empty values are load-bearing: the absent-equals-empty rule of sections 3.1 and 8.1 does not apply to an application key, so the round trip catches a reader or writer that drops a key because its value is null or empty. Reverse-DNS form is guidance a reader must not validate, so `waypoints.` and `.` are application keys; the value under `waypoints.` would be an unusable waypoint, and no rule of the format applies inside it. The `importance` of 99 inside app.viatrail.rulesets is outside 1 to 5 and must survive untouched for the same reason. Dotted keys also sit inside the three opaque objects of section 3.10 (a data record body, a style, and an application key's value, nested two deep in com.example.nested), where they are carried and not reported: the top-level-only rule of section 3.9 does not reach inside an opaque object. Application keys have no entry in counts, so the tree comparison is the only check on them.
